transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start time: 04:00 PM PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Oliver Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Sara Martinez (Nova Retail - Head of ML), Rajiv Kapoor (Nova - Platform Eng), Emily Zhao (Nova - CTO)

Summary (auto): Console walkthrough focused on usage analytics and cost breakdown. Discussed per-route dashboards, token-level cost, batching and caching optimizations, and pilot next steps.

[00:00] Oliver Chen: Okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. This is Oliver from Redwood, with Maya on the call. Quick agenda — we'll walk the Console usage analytics, show per-route dashboards and the token-level cost breakdown, then discuss optimization suggestions and pilot scope.
[00:22] Sara Martinez: Hey thanks, yeah we just want to understand how we'd spot expensive routes and how to attribute cost back to product teams.
[00:31] Maya Patel: Totally, we'll show an example later. Quick note, my audio might cut for a sec — I'm on a spotty hotel wifi.
[01:10] Rajiv Kapoor: Cool. To set context — we send about 5M requests/month today, split across search and chat, peaks to about 250 qps. Sensitive PII only on support-chat route.
[01:35] Emily Zhao: Our main asks are predictability on cost, SLA for latency, and ability to run a private deployment if needed.
[02:05] Oliver Chen: Great, we'll show both hosted and dedicated tradeoffs. Real quick demo — sharing my screen now.
[03:12] Speaker 1: (screen share) Ok this is the Console home, top banner shows overall tokens and spend. The per-route dashboard is here under Routes -> Usage.
[03:40] Maya Patel: You'll notice we index each route with tags, product owner, and sensitivity level — that lets you filter costs by team. Here's a search route, you can see requests, avg latency, p50/p95, and tokens per call.
[04:18] Sara Martinez: Hmm tokens per call — how do you measure that with streaming responses? Sometimes we stream partial responses.
[04:30] Maya Patel: Yes good question, we show both estimated token count and actual measured tokens when finalization occurs. Streaming has minor estimation noise, like +/– 2–3 tokens per call.
[05:05] Oliver Chen: And the cost breakdown — we expose unit cost per model variant and quantization profile; the dashboard multiplies tokens by unit cost and by route filters to show per-route spend.
[05:38] Rajiv Kapoor: What about caching and batching, can we see savings?
[05:50] Maya Patel: Yep, under Optimization -> Cost Impact you'll get an estimated savings view if you enable prefix caching or increase batch sizes. For example, our demo tenant shows 18% reduction with caching on the search route.
[06:30] Speaker 2: (inaudible) quantizashun profiles, what was that?
[06:36] Maya Patel: Sorry, quantization profiles — we support int8-like profiles and mixed-precision. Some noise in the transcript there.
[07:10] Emily Zhao: If we go Dedicated, does that change unit cost?
[07:20] Oliver Chen: Dedicated is priced on reserved capacity + lower per-token compute costs in many cases; the dashboard can simulate monthly spend for hosted vs dedicated given your traffic.
[08:02] Sara Martinez: Can you show an example for a single route?
[08:15] Maya Patel: Sure — clicking into /support-chat — you see a breakdown: requests by day, avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, billing lines (model, compute, storage). Also a 'cost driver' panel that flags long completions or high-temperature calls.
[08:58] Rajiv Kapoor: The flagged 'cost driver' looks useful. Is that rule engine configurable?
[09:10] Maya Patel: Yes you can create thresholds — e.g., if avg completion tokens > 150 for 24h trigger an alert and create a ticket.
[10:00] Speaker 1: (minor overlap) uh we also have route-level RBAC so only product owners see cost details for their route.
[10:22] Oliver Chen: On the billing side, we provide token-level granularity logs exportable to your S3 or to BI. That lets finance do exact chargebacks.
[10:45] Sara Martinez: Export format? parquet or csv?
[10:50] Maya Patel: Parquet preferred for large volumes, but CSV is available. The export includes model, route, tokens, timestamp, and cost columns.
[11:30] Emily Zhao: Security question — will these logs contain sensitive user text? We need to keep PII out.
[11:40] Oliver Chen: We have redaction at ingestion and you can opt-out of request body retention. For private deployments you can keep logs in your VPC and control KMS keys.
[12:05] Rajiv Kapoor: How does KV cache look in console? We heard about K-V cash earlier in the doc, sorry — what metrics do you show?
[12:18] Maya Patel: (laugh) K-V cache metrics: hit rate, miss rate, avg retrieval latency, and token savings from cache hits. We also recommend prefix caching for LLM chat history.
[13:00] Sara Martinez: For pilot scope — we'd want to run search route and support-chat for 2 weeks. Can you simulate projected cost?
[13:12] Oliver Chen: Yes, we have a 'simulate' feature. If you upload 2 weeks of logs or just attach a sample traffic pattern, the Console will run an estimate comparing hosted, dedicated and different quant profiles.
[14:00] Maya Patel: Example here — with your sample profile we estimate $X/month on hosted, $~0.9X on dedicated after reserved commit assumptions. (note: placeholder numbers in demo)
[14:35] Speaker 3: (unintelligible) 
[15:05] Emily Zhao: On SLOs — can you set per-route latency SLOs and alert?
[15:15] Oliver Chen: Yes per-route SLOs inbound to the Console, alerting hooks to PagerDuty or email. Also automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency/SLOs are at risk.
[15:50] Rajiv Kapoor: Fallbacks — does that preserve context?
[15:58] Maya Patel: We do seamless KV cache translation for compatible models; if the model family is different there may be some context resume costs. We usually recommend canary for fallbacks.
[16:35] Sara Martinez: Our regulatory team will want SOC2 and SOC2 Type II evidence and ISO docs.
[16:45] Oliver Chen: We'll email the SOC2 pack; we also have enterprise options for private deployment with audit logs and HSM integration.
[17:20] Maya Patel: small caveat — sometimes model names in the UI get truncated; it's a minor UI bug that devs are tracking.
[17:50] Speaker 1: (laughs) typical.
[18:10] Oliver Chen: Let's walk through a quick live calc. I click 'Cost Estimator', choose search route, set qps and payload, pick model xxl-8q (demo), and the estimator shows tokens * unit price + infra overhead.
[19:00] Sara Martinez: Can we override tokenizer assumptions? We use a custom tokenizer for some NLP models.
[19:12] Maya Patel: Right now we support standard BPE/GPT-style tokenizers; custom tokenizer support is on the roadmap — we can capture that as a requirement.
[20:00] Rajiv Kapoor: For the pilot, we also want to measure 95th percentile latency under peak. Can Redwood run a benchmark with our request traces?
[20:12] Oliver Chen: Yes, we can run a bench using your traces — Maya will own the benchmark run on the demo tenant or on Dedicated if you want to spin up reserved nodes.
[21:00] Maya Patel: I'll need the sample traces and expected concurrency. We'll also set the KV cache scenario — cold vs warm — to show delta.
[22:40] Speaker 2: (brief crosstalk) uh sorry, my mic.
[23:10] Emily Zhao: A quick question on cost attribution: can we map cost back to feature flags or A/B test buckets?
[23:25] Maya Patel: We support custom tags per request — you can pass feature_flag or experiment_id in metadata and the per-route dashboard can pivot by those tags.
[24:00] Oliver Chen: Also worth mentioning Redwood Optimize suggestions — the Console will recommend quant profiles or batching targets to hit cost targets while maintaining quality. It's an automated rule engine that suggests configs.
[25:30] Sara Martinez: How do we validate quality regressions when changing quantization?
[25:45] Maya Patel: We tie suggestions to eval sets and diff test results; the Console will show quality delta on a sample prompt set so you can see BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics or human label snapshots.
[26:30] Rajiv Kapoor: Any limitations on embeddings or reranking metrics in the dashboard?
[26:45] Maya Patel: Embeddings usage shows cosine similarity distribution and index size; reranking is tracked as a separate metric with per-call compute.
[27:30] Oliver Chen: Back to action items — we'll provide the security pack, a small demo tenant, and a cost model spreadsheet.
[28:20] Maya Patel: I'll also put together a recommended configuration — batch sizes, cache TTLs, and quant profiles for your two routes.
[29:00] Sara Martinez: Timing — we need vendor security review complete by mid-April. That workstream includes legal and infra.
[29:12] Oliver Chen: Understood. We'll aim to have the docs and demo tenant before April 1 to give you time for evaluation.
[30:00] Emily Zhao: One more — do you have examples of customers who've saved >20% with Optimize?
[30:12] Maya Patel: Yes, we have case studies — BrightScale saw ~22% savings on search after applying prefix caching and switching to a quantized variant for late-aggregate batches. We'll link the case study.
[31:05] Speaker 3: (some typing)
[32:00] Rajiv Kapoor: On billing, is there a way to allocate infra overhead to teams?
[32:12] Oliver Chen: You can set allocation rules in FinOps — e.g., 70% to product A, 30% to infra if a route uses shared infra. The exported billing lines include an allocation_id so finance can automate chargebacks.
[33:00] Maya Patel: Quick demo note — sometimes the top-level spend ticker lags by a few minutes; it's near-real-time but not strictly live.
[34:20] Sara Martinez: fine. We'll accept a slight delay.
[35:12] Emily Zhao: For private deployment, what's the onboarding timeline?
[35:25] Oliver Chen: Typical private deployment with on-prem or VPC takes 6–8 weeks including security review, infra provisioning, and validation. Dedicated hosted reserved capacity can be <2 weeks.
[36:05] Rajiv Kapoor: What about key management? KMS vs HSM?
[36:15] Maya Patel: We integrate with cloud KMS and optionally HSM for enterprise. You control keys for private deployments.
[37:00] Speaker 2: (garbled)
[38:10] Oliver Chen: Alright, last section — pilot success criteria. Suggested: validate cost delta <=10% vs estimate, p95 latency <200ms for search route, and no data retention of PII for support-chat.
[39:00] Sara Martinez: That sounds reasonable.
[40:20] Maya Patel: I'll prepare the pilot runbook with test cases and data handling checklist.
[41:00] Oliver Chen: Any more questions?
[41:10] Emily Zhao: Not from me.
[41:20] Rajiv Kapoor: None.
[41:30] Sara Martinez: Quick ask — can we get sample dashboards with our branding?
[41:45] Maya Patel: Yes we can apply a CSS skin for enterprise customers in the demo tenant.
[42:10] Oliver Chen: Recap of next steps — Oliver to send pricing and cost model spreadsheet; Maya to provision demo tenant and run initial benchmark; Sara to share traffic and sensitive route list.
[43:00] Emily Zhao: Great, thanks everyone.
[43:12] Speaker 1: (call wrap, thanks)
[47:30] End of recording: ~48 minutes

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-attributions and small ASR errors (quantizashun -> quantization, K-V cash -> KV cache). References to pricing numbers in demo are placeholders.
